basis: Intellectual disability and language delay define this neurodevelopmental disorder; dysmorphic features do not establish other organ damage.
Antenatal enterovirus infection; no specific organ damage is established for at least 30% across this concept.
Intrahepatic duct dilatation and congenital hepatic fibrosis define the syndrome; associated ARPKD is a separate disease despite frequent renal annotations.
Microcephaly and corpus callosum dysgenesis define brain involvement; defining cleft lip/palate affects the oral cavity.
ZIC2-related forebrain malformation; orofacial cleft occurs in 7/69, and endocrine dysfunction lacks a qualifying frequency.
Visual release hallucinations constitute a neurologic syndrome; underlying visual loss has separately diagnosed ocular or cerebral causes.
Cleft lip/palate and sensorineural hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%; hypotelorism does not establish eye damage; central apnea is neurologic.
Nasopharyngeal tumor; proptosis and diplopia in 30-79% support functionally significant orbital occupation; intracranial extension is a minority feature.
Spastic paraplegia with structural scoliosis in 1/1 and sensorineural hearing impairment in 1/2 reported patients; estimates rest on a very small cohort.
Site-variable carcinoma with pancreatic and appendiceal origins in the gastrointestinal axis; ovarian origin has no axis; pulmonary origin is uncommon.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia is a motor-pathway disorder; the IFIH1 gene alone does not establish immune-mediated disease or other organ damage.
Flexion contractures occur in 2/3; ventricular septal defect and optic disc hypoplasia each in 1/3; estimates derive from a small reported cohort.
Vertebral/rib segmentation defects cause thoracic restriction with respiratory insufficiency in 80-99%; nonspecific immune annotation does not prove immunodeficiency.
Inherited dystrophy of the corneal endothelium and Descemet membrane; manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder causing QT prolongation and arrhythmia; pulmonary embolism is a minority complication.
Retinal dystrophy arising in Bruch's membrane; broad neurovascular ancestry does not establish systemic vascular or neurologic damage.
Tumor arises in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside these axes; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
OPTN-related open-angle glaucoma damages the ocular optic nerve; no additional organ involvement is established.
A psychiatric sexual disorder without intrinsic damage to an organ covered by the axes.
Malignant vascular endothelial tumor arising in the mediastinum; mediastinal location alone does not establish lung involvement.
Carcinoma originates in the bulbourethral accessory reproductive gland; urethral ancestry alone does not establish urinary tract origin or damage.
Enlargement of the thyroid gland; swallowing or breathing symptoms do not establish common direct gastrointestinal or pulmonary damage.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; encephalopathy, regression and movement abnormalities characterize the usual Leigh-like phenotype, exceeding 30%.
Muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%; optic atrophy/visual loss in 30-79%; respiratory failure reflects neuromuscular weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Inherited motor-neuron disorder with defining proximal lower-limb muscle wasting and weakness in most patients; developmental delay occurs in only 5-29%.
